newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 25.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The ruling coalition garnered a majority of the senatorial seats with 52 out of 81 possible. The Social Democrats came away with 25 seats. The elections were overshadowed by a disappointingly low voter turnout of only 30.6 percent.
- The Czech crown will not be affected by the senatorial election results and should remain stable next year as well, according to the head economist for bank IPB.
- A huge explosion followed by an extensive fire and gas explosions shook a rafinery belonging to Ceska Rafinerska at Chemopetrol Litvinov shortly after midnight on Saturday.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The ability of domestic companies to repay debts has worsened year-by-year since the beginning of the reform process. In the middle of this year there were 86.5 billion crowns worth of overdue loans in industry: 13.6 billion crowns were owed by construction companies. This is an increase of 13.1 percent in industry and nearly 50 percent in construction over the middle of 1995.

PRAVO - In the first three quarters of the year trading with Germany, Italy and Great Britain showed the greatest downturn. The Czech Republic posted a trade surplus of five billion crowns with Germany after nine months in 1995. After three quarters of 1996 there was a deficit of 5.6 billion crowns, a decrease of 10.6 billion crowns. The deficit with Italy increased by 8.9 billion crowns to 17.8 billion crowns while the deficit with Great Britain increased by 5.9 billion crowns to 9.9 billion crowns in the same period.
- Vitkovice a.s. expects losses of 300 million crowns this year instead of the originally predicted profits of 500 million crowns, according to Vit Obdrzalek from Vitkovice.

- The Czech National Bank, in its proposal for the privatisation of the four largest Czech banks, has recommended management changes in order to significantly strengthen the state's ownership rights in these banks.

- ICEC Ostrava began the production of paper in Slovakia's Vidim paper plant, accordin to the press spokesman for ICEC, Vaclav Andrysek. ICEC obtained the Slovak plant in an auction for 35.5 million marks.

- In the first three quarters of this year there were 128,048 building permits, 4.5 percent more than in the same period a year ago. New construction accounted for 54.4 percent of the permits with the remainder for reconstruction and modernisation. The expected value of the construction is 151.211 billion crowns.

- There is currently one chemist's shop for every 6,000-7,000 Czechs, compared with one for every 15,000 people in 1989. The number of chemist's shops reached 1,800 and is not expected to increase further, according to the vice-chairman of Naturprodukt, Jan Machura.
